title: End of the Sun
subtitle: A pitch-black ship, enveloped in storm, rain, and hatred.

items.text: The sound of scraping metal brings an end to the pumping rock music, painting a look of solemnity and fear on the faces of every guest.
A lithe figure steps gracefully onto the stage.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: We should raise a toast. One and all.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: For we're in luck's good graces to be aboard this ship.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: A ship, hmm, perhaps one ought to think of it more as an ark.
The guests exchange uneasy glances. After a long silence, one guest hesitantly breaks the silence with a question.

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: Just what are you getting at?

items.speaker: Guest II
items.text: Oh, I get it! Is this some kind of surprise theme party, like a murder mystery?! Is that right, Ms. Barcarola?
Barcarola looks bewildered. The captain's sudden and strange appearance on the stage was certainly not part of any performance. At least, not one she had prepared.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: No, I didn't plan for any of this.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: You aren't entirely wrong though, Mr. Matthews, for this is certainly a surprise, if not so much a party as a ceremony.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Allow me to congratulate you, our honored guests. Each of you, with your unique talents, resources, and powerful connections, have earned a chance to join Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Guest II
items.text: If this is some kind of joke, Captain, I don't find it funny! So how about you knock it off!

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: There's no joke at all. Unless you plan on throwing away your precious opportunity to join us in the new era.

items.speaker: Guest II
items.text: What the hell is that supposed to mean? Have you gone insane!?
In their fear and anger, the guests make to leave, but a young man in a mask swiftly blocks the doorway.

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: How dare you blaspheme our savior?!

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: Toa, ever since you put on that mask, you've been acting strangely, like a different person.
She can hardly recognize her dear friend at all.

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: You're wrong, Selone! I was lost after we left Meli. But now, I've never felt so certain of myself.

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: You must ready yourself for the mask trial, too. We must all be willing to sacrifice to bring our people into the new era!
He proudly pounds his chest as he glares disdainfully at the trembling crowd before him.

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: As for these ignorant outsiders, hmph, they will never understand the depth of the crimes they've committed or the punishment they deserve!

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: Calm down, Toa. Don't bother with these outsiders. They only care about themselves.

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: Only the "Storm" can bring the change we need.
With bizarre masks, fervent prophecies, and the clinking of misshapen shells, they perform their unannounced stage play.
Its "audience" cowers together in fear.

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: Lunatics!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, it seems as though the islanders aboard are working with Manus Vindictae!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There's no telling what else the Manus have up their sleeve. We need to call for support as soon as possible.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: But our communications are jammed.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Regulus, are you able to reach Mr. Ulrich?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I should be. I've got no clue where he's at now. He dashed off with the roaring machine, mumbling something about "sound wave frequency" and "nuclide R."

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Still, I might as well give it a shot, if I can still recall Laplace's internal frequency, that is.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto, we must calm the situation before things escalate further.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: On it!
Orders are issued methodically.
Grace watches with interest as a navy top hat moves through the crowd. A gentle smile creeps across her face.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Ladies and gentlemen.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Perhaps you have yet to understand what the "Storm" really is.

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: No, perhaps we don't. Because I remember what you wrote in all the flyers!

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: The "Free Breeze" is equipped with a double-hull and the most advanced communication systems available, capable of contacting rescue and support under any circumstances.

items.speaker: Guest II
items.text: Yeah, and something about a stabilizing system. Why should we be worried about some heavy weather?

items.speaker: Guest II
items.text: Or were you lying to us?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Oh, the specifications of the ship are all very much true. No natural weather phenomenon could endanger us here.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: However, the "Storm" I speak of is not a mere matter of churning wind and thunder. And no double-hull nor stabilizing system could stand against it.

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: So, what the hell is this "Storm"?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: It is a cleansing—a deluge that will come to eradicate all the sickness of this world.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: And an opportunity, a chance to reverse our course. All that is asked of you is an insignificant price.

items.speaker: Guest II
items.text: Reverse? Price? What are you talking about?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: In the '90s, veins turned into wires. In the '80s, skulls turned into geometric shapes. Oh, and the '60s, what fun we had then!

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: The entire world became a pop art spectacle!

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: And Manus Vindictae have seen us through each one, for all these many years.
The crowd's murmuring grows louder and more chaotic.

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: So, you're saying that the world is going to be transformed?

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: And something weird will happen to our bodies, too?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: You're exactly right.

items.speaker: Guest II
items.text: And the Manus were behind all of this? Why?!

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Now, now, don't be so harsh on us. We've made heroic efforts to cleanse this world of its sickness.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: But each generation keeps making the same mistakes: economic collapse, environmental crisis, endless wars and bloodshed ...

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: We had no choice. The wounds of this world must be cleansed. One deluge at a time. Now, we are welcoming a new "Storm."

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: One that will reverse us to an even more distant past.
Fear and anger intertwine. The crowd is like a volcano on the verge of eruption.

items.speaker: Guest III
items.text: You're a lunatic, Captain. You need your head examined.

items.speaker: Guest III
items.text: Lady, you need a psychiatrist!

items.speaker: Guest IV
items.text: But these things you're showing us ... they really happened?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: No need to take my word for it. You will all bear witness to it soon.
The crowd descends into a hushed panic. Every lapping of the waves can be heard amid their almost ghostly murmurs.
This is the perfect moment to calm the crowd.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The "Storm" is NOT coming.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We are from the St. Pavlov Foundation—

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: An organization dedicated to the protection and rights of humans and arcanists.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Huh.

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: Ah, thank goodness!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: As the Timekeeper of the St. Pavlov Foundation, I can assure you:

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What she showed you won't happen here. Manus Vindictae are just trying to manipulate you into buying into their deception and hatred. Don't give in to this false fear!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Please, everyone, remain calm.
Another bamboo arrow shoots through the air.

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: Protect us? You? Don't make me laugh!
Fatutu doesn't hesitate to stop him.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Toa, wait!

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: She seems trustworthy. Maybe we should listen to what they have to say.

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: Really? You think these people care about rebuilding our home?

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: Were they there when Nukutaeao was hit by the great waves? Where was their protection then?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I'm not sure, but I just can't bear the thought that we might make a decision we'll regret later. I don't wanna see any more cracks and scratches on our shells.
Her cries cannot overpower the murmuring of the guests, nor can they quell the rising fury of her kin.
And they certainly cannot stop another poison arrow.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: *Ed  è  sübito  sera——！

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: This is getting out of hand. Be careful, Timekeeper. They're coming for us!
The hall is in utter disarray.
Labored breathing, sighs, and sobbing blend together like a sickly pot of thick stew.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: No. This isn't right.
She wants to say more, but the familiar scent of herbal incense suddenly overwhelms her.
Sleepy Reeds—a herbal anesthetic used by Nukutai priests during surgeries.

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: I think you need some rest, sister.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: I'm sorry, Fatutu. This needs to be done.
Selone catches her as she falls unconscious.
The ongoing confrontation on the other side of the hall is evidently far more intense.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: A fine speech, Ms. Vertin, such delectable righteous indignation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Surrender, Ms. Grace. Your lies will not succeed here.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Why, of course. To tell a lie brings the harshest of consequences, even a kindergartener knows that.
Grace surveys the hall. Countless eyes are fixed on her.
Anger, hostility, confusion, disdain—she has walked through it all before and never left a trace.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Everyone, whenever there's an imminent "Storm," my watch here starts a countdown, but there have been no signs of—
Grace places a delicate hand on her raised arm, interrupting her speech.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: What a coincidence, Ms. Vertin. I so happen to have a similar device myself.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Three.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Two.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: One.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Impossible!

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Ms. Vertin.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: As you said, lies will not succeed here. The question is, who here is the liar?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Ladies and gentlemen, I invite you to relish the sight before you.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Here we are ...

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: The last evening on earth.
